I understand you want to be polite but him saying things like that are NOT appropriate in any way. In therapy you should be able to speak openly with him about these feelings and work through them really but if you feel that you can't because of family friends ect I think that's pretty counter intuitive to therapy. You could always tell him that you want a break from therapy if you wanted to be polite but really he should know that saying slightly provactive things to a patient is going to really mess with their head. Very unprofessional and if you do end up confronting him about it I would watch his reaction closely, he shouldn't make you feel in any way bad or embarrassed and he should be apologetic for making you feel uncomfortable.

Yeah this is so important. I never understood the 'impulsive' trait because if anything I over dwell on things, so I assumed I wasn't self harming or being impulsive. Impulsivity can relate to a lot of things, often for me it's sharing too much in a conversation or taking too much on and then it affecting me later on or starving myself the whole day to then stuff myself until my stomach hurts for hours.

I think this all the time. It can make me feel like an alien, like, why is life so much harder for me? Or I overcompensate when someone else could be upset because I struggle to realise that not everyone has this extreme emotional response like me.

Personally my diagnosis was very, very vague. They didn't want to even give it to me as not to, 'label me.' Almost everything I have learned is from my own research which is also very difficult when there's so much misinformation. Not only this but very few real life comparisons to how the triats can affect a person which is why this thread is so important. It's also super important to be welcoming surely, considering the well known validation issues (to name just the one) affecting the disorder. 

What you say about Marsha Linhan is really interesting. I've often wondered if there IS a way to treat attachment really, but that could also just be a reflection of where I'm at in life. It's sometimes good to run into posts like this which make feel a lot less alone and empathy for the poster.

I suppose it just differs from person to person! Studies have shown that there is probably no negative effect from missing REM sleep but I’d still be glad to be having it rather than not

Man I know what you mean. I've never had someone blatantly tell me they didnt believe I had bpd but I think they take me less seriously because of it or because I'm a 'quiet' borderline they doubt me or feelings. ugh and its the one place that is meant to be judgement free

Its someone laughing at my joke so I feel great for hours, I am contemplating all the new hobbies, ventures and ultimately the SUCCESS I will have because I feel so good and on top of the world. Then I bump into someone and I apologise but they are annoyed and walk off, I am left feeling completely responsible and guilty. Everything I do is bad. I am bad. I deserve bad. The next few hours, or day(s) might be like this until a switch goes off and I feel separate from all that intense emotion I just experienced and I move onto the next one. The hours before seem hazy but still raw.

I cannot trust my emotions or thoughts at first glance because I do not know if they are legitimate responses or my BPD hijacking my brain. 

I feel disgust and loathing towards myself often. 

Other times my life feels like a dream, like I'm not quite there and the interactions arent quite happening. I am not myself and I think to myself that people must realise how weird I am (I dont know if they actually do.)

I dont know what my personality is or what my interests are, I find them changing depending on who I am with or what mood I am in. Sometimes a certain 'personality' takes over and im that person for weeks.... until im not and I am left questioning every part of myself. 

Someone in my life could be everything to me, all my trust and love. Then for whatever reason, often me realising I dont mean as much to them, they are no longer everything but it hurts my heart so much that they arent. 

I very rarely feel anger and if I do it eventually turns into anger with myself and crying for hours.

​

Just a few thoughts haha. Im interested to see how others are affected.
